analytic.title: Energy-Efficient Task Allocation for VFI-based Real-Time Multi-Core Systems

application.desc: GROBID - A machine learning software for extracting information from scholarly documents

div.p: Chip Multiprocessor (CMP) has become computing engine for a wide spectrum of applications due to its higher throughput and better energy efficiency. The problem of optimal task-to-core allocation with the minimum energy consumption has been proven to be NP-hard. In order to solve the energy-efficient real-time task mapping in the voltagefrequency islands (VFI) based multicore system, we propose a heuristics EEGA (Energy-Efficient and Genetic Algorithm) to address the problem. During the iteration process of the algorithm, the energy consumption of the processor can be gradually optimized by the selection, crossover and mutation operators. Experimental results show that when compared with other energy-efficient mapping algorithms, our proposed approach can gain better performance with regard to the energy efficiency and schedulability ratio.

div.head: INTRODUCTION
div.p: In these days, with the technology scales and device integration level increases in chip manufacture, the power consumption has become one of the key challenges and critical constraints in the design of future high-performance processors. Some solutions have been proposed to mitigate the energy pressure. Chip Multi-Processor (CMP), which integrates several processing units in one chip, allows the throughput increase at affordable power [1]. Moreover, dynamic voltage and frequency scaling (DVFS) is a framework to change the operating voltage and frequency based on the performance requirement on the fly. Generally, the resources, especially the processor, in real-time systems are not fully and effectively utilized. Thus, the dynamic slack can be exploited for energy reduction. DVFS has been widely used to optimize the energy consumption in both embedded real-time systems and high performance server systems. Many literatures have been proposed with respect to DVFS energy aware scheduling in real-time systems [2,3].

However, conventional globally synchronized clocking CMP systems have been increasingly difficult to design. In order to better support the flexible power management for CMP systems, voltage and frequency island (VFI) technique has been studied recently. VFI is comprised of a group of processing cores which are powered by the same voltage. Instead of the chip-level voltage supply, different VFIs in the same multicore processor can operate at different voltage supplies. In the VFI-based CMP system, processing cores are partitioned into groups and all cores in each group share the same operating voltage and have the same processing frequency [4,5].

There is considerable amount of literature on the energyefficient designs in real-time multi-core and multi-processor systems. In [6], Aydin et al. address the energy aware scheduling of periodic hard real-time tasks, and give static offline solution and on-line speed reduction mechanism to compute the optimal speed and dynamically reclaim energy, respectively. In [7], the problem of partitioning periodic realtime tasks onto a multiprocessor platform is proved to be NP-hard. Further, the Worst-Fit-Decreasing (WFD) task partition heuristics is shown to be better than other heuristic algorithms. Bautista et al. proposed an energy-efficient algorithm to utilize DVS to schedule real-time tasks in the multi-core system [8]. But they aim at soft real-time applications. Seo et al. proposed a dynamic re-partition algorithm to balance the loads between the processor cores at runtime, such that the energy consumption can be reduced [9]. But they assumed the processor have the limitation that all cores must run at the same performance level. That is, all processing cores in a chip must operate at the same clock frequency and operating voltage.

The majority of the previous researches are either concentrating on per-core DVFS, (i.e., each processing unit can operate at different voltage/frequency), or consider the full-chip DVFS, i.e., all cores on the chip must operate at the same voltage/frequency [10]. In [10], Kong et al. studied the real-time task partition in the Multicore system where the processing cores are organized into VFIs. However, they assumed that the operating frequency of each VFI can be adjusted continuously between the minimum and the maximum frequency of the processor.

In this paper, we will study the energy aware real-time task allocation problem in the multi-core system where voltage/frequency island architecture is adopted. A heuristics EEGA, i.e., energy-efficient and genetic algorithm based real-time tasks allocation, is presented to solve the problem. The rest of this paper is organized as follows: Section introduces the system modes and defines the target problem. Section presents the algorithm in detail. Section provides experiment results for performance evaluation of the proposed algorithm, while Section V concludes the paper.

div.head: D. Problem Definition
div.p: Given a set Γ of periodic real-time tasks and a VFIbased homogeneous multicore platform M ,which is comprised of nc processing cores
div.formula: nc c c c ,... ,2 1
div.p: , the energyefficient task allocation problem addressed in this paper is defined as following: mapping the given tasks onto processing cores and determining the executing frequency for each core subject to the limitation of the VFI-level frequency synchronization, such that the overall energy consumption is minimized.

The periodic real-time task partition that results in minimum energy consumption has been proved to be NPhard [7]. As it is difficult to derive the optimal solution in polynomial time, we will develop a heuristics based on genetic algorithms to solve this problem.

div.head: D. Selection, Crossover And Mutation Operations
div.p: In each step of the inheritance process, a new generation will be produced from the previous population. Better solutions have more opportunity to survive during the selection step. In this paper, the roulette wheel approach is utilized to select chromosomes to build a new generation. In this method, all chromosomes in the old population are placed on a roulette wheel according as their fitness. Each chromosome is assigned a segment of roulette wheel whose size is proportional to the value of its fitness. Then, new chromosomes are selected one by one from the previous population. div.head: IV. PERFORMANCE EVALUATION
div.p: In order to evaluate the performance of the proposed allocation algorithm, we implement EEGA and compare it with two other energy-efficient real-time task allocation algorithms, i.e., the conventional WFD heuristic and the LTF algorithm [10]. The experiment is conducted in the environment with Windows Server 2003, and the algorithms are implemented in Visual C++ 2008 express.

The parameters used in our power mode can be found in [9]. The target CMP consist of 8 cores and these cores are uniformly divided into 4 VFIs, i.e., each VFI contains 2 processing core. We assume that there are 6 levels of supply voltage for the processor: {0.6V, 0.7V, 0.8V, 0.9V, 1.0V, 1.1V}. The task sets are randomly generated and the size nt is uniformly distributed in the range of [16,40]

). The parameters of the proposed algorithm are set as follows: population size m =1000, max iteration number mit =500, crossover probability cp =0.8, mutation probability mp =0.05. For each case, we generate 1000 task sets and the result data is the average of these 1000 task sets. Fig. 2 gives the outline of the energy consumption of the three algorithms over the average core utilization (denoted as acu ). The energy is normalized to that of the WFD mapping. As can be seen from Fig. 2, the WFD allocation uses most energy, while EEGA can effectively reduce the energy consumption. Fig. 3 depicts the schedulability rates of the three schemes. The schedulability rate is defined as the ratio of the number of schedulable task sets to 1000 (note that we generated 1000 task sets for each case in the experiment). As shown in Fig. 3, when the average core utilization acu is low, the rates under all algorithms are equivalent, and they are all close to 1. Nevertheless, when acu is high, e.g., 8 . 0 > acu , EEGA shows better schedulability performance. Specially, when acu =0.9, the schedulability rate of EEGA is 8% higher that those of WFD and LTF.

div.head: V. CONCLUSIONS
div.p: With the increasing of processor speed and its performance, processor power consumption and heat dissipation have become critical challenges in the design of high-performance systems. Many solutions have been proposed to relieve the energy pressure. Multicore (or chiplevel multiprocessor) architecture has been brought forward and been widely used to mitigate the energy pressure. Moreover, VFI (voltage-frequency island)-based multicore platform could give more flexible energy management. VFI supports different executing speeds and voltage supplies for different VFIs such that the clock speed can be reduced and the energy consumption could be effectively saved.

In this paper, we study the energy-efficient periodic realtime allocation problem over the VFI-based chip multiprocessor platform with DVFS. We propose a heuristics, energy-efficient and genetic algorithm based real-time tasks allocation, i.e., EEGA, to obtain the near-optimal solution. The proposed algorithm takes the VFI-level frequency synchronization into consideration, and struggles to allocate the real-time tasks onto processor cores such that the schedulability of the tasks can be satisfied, and the total energy consumption can be reduced. Experimental results show that, compared with other algorithms, EEGA could improve the energy efficiency by consumes less energy and has better schedulability performance.
